title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has answered the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and public standards by pledging to create clearer ethical guidelines, tighten regulatory oversight, and boost transparency in AI use. It stresses working closely with industry, academia, and international partners to make AI systems safe, trustworthy, and in line with public values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has issued guidelines to regulate how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and qualifications, aiming to protect fairness, reliability, and the integrity of assessment processes. The guidance was released after a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science and Business to ensure AI tools meet regulatory standards in the education sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright laws impact the development and use of AI systems, especially when these systems learn from copyrighted works. It assesses the legal, economic, and ethical consequences and offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” acknowledging the urgency of AI governance. It outlines new measures to strengthen regulation, foster innovation, and address ethical, safety, and workforce impacts of AI technologies across the country.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will examine how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It also includes a FAQ section to help stakeholders understand the committee’s process and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee about how artificial intelligence should be governed. The submission highlights concerns about regulation, ethics, and best practices for AI development and deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how artificial intelligence technologies are reshaping the oversight, testing, and approval processes for medical products. It proposes applying the guidelines from the AI White Paper to ensure these products remain safe, effective, and transparent for patients and regulators.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑enabled defence body for its size. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, streamlining operations, fostering stakeholder confidence, and boosting strategic influence in the defence sector.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The plan explains how the UK Department for Transport will partner with transport companies to use AI to make travel faster, safer, and greener. It also sets out how the government will monitor for risks such as privacy, safety, and fairness and create rules to keep AI use responsible.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report outlines how AI developers are accessing and using copyrighted materials, as governed by Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It tracks progress, identifies challenges, and offers recommendations to ensure legal compliance while fostering AI innovation.
